title: Cognitive boundaries and theta phase precession: human microwire LFP during movie-clip encoding, scene recognition and time discrimination (Zheng et al. 2024, DANDI 000940)
description: An iEEG-BIDS representation of microwire local field potentials recorded from Behnke-Fried depth electrodes in 16 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Recordings were made in the amygdala, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus and some frontal sites during a cognitive-boundary memory paradigm: encoding of silent movie clips with no, soft or hard event boundaries, followed by scene-recognition and time-discrimination tests. The data support analyses of theta phase precession and episodic memory formation and retrieval. They were converted from the authors' NWB release on DANDI (000940) without altering signal values.
methods_description: Microwire LFPs were recorded at 32 kHz (0.1-8000 Hz, Neuralynx ATLAS) and downsampled by the authors to 200 Hz. The NWB ElectricalSeries was written to BrainVision float32 microvolts without filtering, re-referencing, cropping or channel removal. Task trials (encoding, scene recognition, time discrimination) and TTL markers were mapped to events.tsv.
